title: Low-power client streaming contracts PRD (draft)
summary: Exploration and proposed PRD for a minimal-cost streaming surface targeted at battery- and CPU-constrained clients (mobile, IoT, browser low-power modes). Focus areas: compact incremental JSON frames, energy-aware handshake, lightweight tool-calling primitives, and SDK ergonomics that minimize wakeups and memory pressure.
background: Customer signals: a set of partners building offline-first mobile companions and embedded assistants ask for a streaming surface that preserves progressive results but fits devices with tight CPU, memory, and network energy budgets. Existing hosted streaming surfaces assume always-on sockets and abundant client compute for parsing and tool orchestration. This doc sketches a product surface and implementation guardrails to serve low-power clients while maintaining tool-calling and structured-output guarantees.
user_stories: As a mobile SDK author I want partial results packaged in tiny, predictable frames so the app can render intermediate suggestions without heavy JSON parsing
As an edge-device integrator I want a handshake that negotiates compression/verbosity levels so devices with sporadic connectivity can request compact payloads
As a solutions engineer I want tool calls to be represented as compact action tokens so the client can defer expensive tool execution to a backend if necessary
As a product manager I want telemetry that attributes token-level energy and latency costs back to customers so we can quantify unit economics for constrained clients
goals: Define a minimal streaming frame envelope for progressive structured output that minimizes client-side CPU and memory allocations
Provide a tiny tool-calling sub-protocol that allows clients to request tool resolution vs. server-side execution with clear semantics
Specify SDK ergonomics (APIs + defaults) that reduce wakeups, avoid large allocations, and support intermittent connectivity
Create observability hooks that capture energy-impact proxies (bytes, parse time, socket wakeups) for billing/optimization
non_goals: Full rewrite of the hosted streaming API: protocol should be backward-compatible and opt-in
Extensive on-device model execution — local inference is out-of-scope
Providing a one-size-fits-all compression scheme; we'll standardize a small set of negotiated options
high_level_solution: Introduce an opt-in 'compact-stream' mode on the Hosted API. Clients negotiate a compact profile during session init. Server emits small atomic frames: header byte (frame type + flags), optional delta-key (short token id), and payload compressed with a negotiated codec. Structured outputs are expressed as shallow key/value frames to avoid deep parse trees. Tool calls are emitted as compact action descriptors with a resolution hint.
protocol_sketch: Session init: POST /v1/sessions with header "compact-stream: profile=lowpower;codec=zstd-lite;verbosity=minimal". Server responds with session-id and supported feature bits. During the session, frames are streamed as base64-safe binary over chunked HTTP/2 or WebTransport; each frame starts with one header byte: bits 0..2=frame type (0=meta,1=text-delta,2=json-kv,3=action,4=checkpoint), bits 3..5=codec, bits 6..7=reserved. Payload length encoded as 1-3 bytes LEB128 to avoid fixed 4-byte fields. json-kv frames carry a short key index (1 byte) and a UTF-8 value; clients maintain a tiny local dictionary negotiated at handshake to avoid repeated key strings. action frames carry action-id (2 bytes), resolution-hint (1 byte: 0=client-prefer,1=server-execute,2=defer), and compact argument blob (max 256B) which can be a short typed payload or a URL to an attachment. Checkpoint frames provide a small opaque marker clients can use to resume if connection drops.
sdk_guidelines: Expose a single compactStream() constructor that returns an async iterator of minimal frames rather than a full JSON document
Provide default profiles: 'lowpower' (minimal keys, zstd-lite, no pretty text), 'balanced' (more keys, zstd, richer payloads)
Parse frames incrementally with a tiny state machine (avoid full JSON.parse on each partial update). Provide language bindings that reuse buffers (ArrayBuffer pools) and expose parse-time metrics

Offer an actionHandler(callback) that receives compact action frames; default handler performs no heavy processing and exposes a 'resolveRemotely()' helper that calls an explicit server-side tool resolution endpoint
Support a lightweight checkpoint API: on reconnect the SDK sends last-seen checkpoint id to fast-forward missed frames
telemetry_and_observability: Emit metrics: frames_received, average_frame_size_bytes, parse_time_ms_p50/p90, socket_wakeups_per_minute (approx), action_resolution_count_by_hint
Label telemetry by compact_profile and device_class (mobile-low, mobile-mid, embedded) to enable cost modeling
Provide a dev-mode flag in SDK that samples raw frames for debugging but defaults to off to avoid energy cost
Correlate tool-call fallbacks and deferred resolutions with downstream latency and energy estimates
perf_targets: Average frame size <= 180 bytes under 'lowpower' for typical token deltas
Client parse time p90 < 8ms on a single-core 800MHz ARM profile for a 200B frame
Socket wakeups reduced by 60% vs naive per-token text streaming by coalescing small deltas into <200ms bursts
Action handshake round-trip for server-execute path < 120ms in same region (SLA candidate)
security_considerations: All frames authenticated using the same session token as hosted API; replay protection via monotonic checkpoint ids
Action frames that include URLs must enforce signed, short-lived attachments and optional content validation before client deref
Avoid exposing sensitive keys in the client-side dictionary; dictionary entries are semantic keys, not secrets
Do not allow arbitrary binary payload execution on client; SDK enforces max arg blob size and typed validation
operational_considerations: Server must maintain a compact-frame encoder path in the runtime with short-key dictionaries per model/route
Edge routing should prefer low-latency regions for 'lowpower' profiles to reduce client radio-on time
Storage for checkpoints should be cheap and sharded; checkpoints are small opaque tokens mapped to sequence positions
We should run A/B experiments to measure battery usage delta on representative devices before GA
open_questions: Should compact frames be binary-first (WebTransport) or text-first (chunked HTTP) to maximize browser compatibility?
What set of keys belong in the default dictionary vs. route-specific dictionary? How to version these safely?
How aggressive should server-side coalescing be before it harms perceived interactivity?
Billing implications: do we charge by bytes, frames, or an energy proxy metric? Need finance input
